svg.title: INOVIXUX — Android status-bar small icon (ic_stat_inovixux)
svg.desc:
Flattened, single-opaque-colour derivative of inovixux-icon-b2c.svg, per docs/brand/13-mobile-app-patterns.md §6.1. Android renders the notification small icon as an ALPHA MASK — every colour, gradient and partial fill is discarded and replaced by the tint passed to setColor(). Three consequences drove this redraw rather than a reuse of the app icon:
1. The gradient is meaningless here, so the mark is drawn in flat #FFFFFF. Only alpha survives. 2. The four corner dots of the app icon sit at opacity 0.5. In an alpha mask that is not a lighter purple — it is a half-transparent hole, which at 24dp (r=1.44px) renders as four grey smudges. Dropped, per §6.1's own "drop it rather than shipping a smudge" rule. 3. The verified-node dot is concentric with the X crossing. Painted flat, node and strokes merge into one blob and the node stops reading as a node. It is kept legible by knocking a 1.1px transparent gap ring out of the X — the arms stop short of the node instead of running under it. That gap is the whole reason this file exists.
Construction rule preserved from 14-icon-system.md §1 / the master mark: round cap, round join, 2.4 stroke on a 24 viewBox (== the source's 2px on a 20 viewBox, scaled 1.2x). Content is inset to a 22dp box (cap edges land at 2.55 and 21.45), matching Android's status-bar icon content-area guidance.
